chapter: Early records, Detroit and Prohibition-era nightlife
title: The Arcadia Ballroom job that closed, then gigging before Chick Webb
summary: Carter's Arcadia job closed within months; he describes the two-stage ballroom, then freelancing through drummer Peekaboo Jimmy's bookings before Chick Webb.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Well, it was on the order of the Roseland Ballroom, but it was built entirely different. It was larger than the Roseland Ballroom and had a stage like -- I don't know whether it had a stage and a balcony that ran around. I don't know whether it was a theater that was, you know, converted into a ballroom or whatever. Anyway, it was a ballroom at that time, and they had two bands, you know. They had two stages, one on each stage.
Yeah. Well, Roseland too had two bands. But then after that, after -- after Benny Carter's band, where did I go?
Well, you were with Chick Webb, weren't you?

Yeah, I guess I did. I think I -- see, like I was getting fairly into the business then and I think I just gigged around for a couple of months or so. Because the business was good at that time. You could leave one job and go on another job or just freelance around with different people. There was a guy named Peekaboo Jimmy. Peekaboo Jimmy was a drummer, and he was a -- and he'd see you and he'd say, 'Well, I've got some gigs for you and he'd take out your book and he'd write all these jobs down, a half a dozen jobs, you know. And then the next job I got I think was with Chick Webb.
